principles: Evidence before claims: readiness cannot be reported as outcome data.
Host-neutral core: workflow and experiment proof are not tied to Codex, Claude, or any single host namespace.
Only fix real correctness boundaries: preserve cell ordering, snapshot binding, and budget-lock discipline.
Default-deny provider execution: external calls require explicit authorization and complete runner metadata.
drivers: M2 readiness is already prepared but provider execution is explicitly disabled.
The next formal execution step is cell 03 calibration; cell 06 sequencing depends on a real budget lock from cell 03.
The user needs a visible milestone table so future sessions know what is complete and what remains blocked.

options.name: direct-phase1-run
pros: Would produce experiment rows sooner if all provider credentials and budget approvals were already available.
cons: Risks spending budget before launch metadata is locked.
Would blur readiness with provider outcome data.
Could violate A2prime sequencing if budget lock is not generated first.

options.name: launch-plan-and-local-gate
pros: Creates a detailed execution document and machine-readable launch artifact.
Keeps provider calls disabled until explicit authorization.
Mechanically preserves cell 03 before cell 06 sequencing.
Gives the user a clear milestone table and next-step state.
cons: Does not by itself produce H-M1/H-M3 experiment results.
Requires a later explicit provider execution authorization to run real cells.

options.name: docs-only-note
cons: Would not provide a local checker or machine-readable launch boundary.
Future agents could still misread readiness as outcome data.

rationale: The correct next step is to convert provider-free readiness into an auditable launch gate and cell 03 calibration path, while keeping provider execution disabled until real snapshots, budget caps, and runner metadata are supplied.

preMortem.scenario: Readiness is mistaken for experiment evidence.
preMortem.trigger: A later agent reads the protocol/status but not the launch boundary.
preMortem.consequence: Paper wording could overclaim H-M1/H-M3 or model-agnostic replication.
preMortem.mitigation: State in the doc, launch artifact, checker, and status table that providerCallsMade=false and no outcome data exists.

preMortem.trigger: Cell 06 is launched before real cell 03 calibration medians exist.
preMortem.consequence: The main H-M1 comparison is invalid or vulnerable to post-hoc budget tuning.
preMortem.mitigation: Checker keeps cell 06 blocked until a real cell-03-derived phase1-budget-lock exists.

preMortem.scenario: Host label is treated as model snapshot.
preMortem.trigger: Runner metadata records Codex CLI or Claude Code CLI as the executor/reviewer snapshot.
preMortem.consequence: Multi-model evidence becomes uninterpretable because host and provider family are mixed.
preMortem.mitigation: Checker rejects host labels in snapshot fields and requires dated provider-family metadata.

preMortem.scenario: Provider execution accidentally happens in this story.
preMortem.trigger: A runner command is added or enabled while writing launch artifacts.
preMortem.consequence: Costs are incurred without explicit human budget authorization and records are not pre-registered.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep providerExecutionAuthorized=false and providerCallEnabled=false in the launch artifact; the story excludes full campaign execution.
